lyrics:
[Intro: stop-start guitar riff, snare hits, building]

[Verse 1: playful, watching, full band]
There he goes, crossing at the light
Newspaper folded, collar right
I've seen that walk before somewhere
Goodness
Well, hello there

[Verse 2: playful, a little bolder]
There he goes, slowing by the shop
Looking in the window, coming to a stop
Is he lost or is he shy?
Say something, don't just stand and sigh

[Growl: spoken aside, riff underneath]
Grrr
Oh, behave

[Bridge: softer, strings, hopeful]
If he turns left, I'll let it be
If he turns right, he's coming for tea
I've got a kettle and a second cup
I've got a lot of time to make up

[Verse 3: band drops, resigned]
There he goes, down toward the square
I should have waved, I should have dared
It's getting late, the bench is cold
Oh well, that's that, I'm far too old

[Break: riff stops, one drum, spoken]
Hang on
Is that his paper?
He's left his paper

[Final Verse: riff returns, full band, delighted]
There he is, turning at the light
Patting his pockets, what a sight
He's crossing over, coming near
Well
Hello there

[Outro: riff, final chord, a laugh]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 127 BPM, 4/4, A major. A confident, strutting beat with a riff that keeps stopping and starting. Playful and suspenseful.

VOICE: Female alto, warm and amused, with good comic timing. She sings the verses as if narrating to herself, drops in a playful growl and spoken asides, softens for the bridge, and sounds delighted at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: An electric guitar playing a twangy, climbing riff that builds a few notes at a time, stops, and starts again. A second guitar doubling it. A snare drum hit hard on every beat. Electric bass. A string section in the bridge. Piano. Handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the riff building in stages. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:36 Verse 2. 0:56 The growl and a spoken aside over the riff. 1:04 Bridge with strings. 1:28 Verse 3, the band drops back. 1:52 Break: the riff stops, one drum, three spoken lines. 2:02 Final verse with the riff and full band. 2:28 Outro, the riff, a final chord and a laugh at 2:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1960s Nashville rock and roll: clean, punchy and bright, guitars twangy, snare loud, a little slapback echo on the voice.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The break at 1:52, when the riff stops and she notices the newspaper.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The watcher is a woman of a certain age, the object of interest has silver hair, and she has 'a lot of time to make up'. The original's fantasy becomes something that could happen on any high street.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Interest, hope, resignation, delight.
